battlecard_summary: Elevator pitch: Redwood Dedicated Autoscaling delivers predictable baseline throughput with configurable burst capacity, enabling predictable SLAs while absorbing short-term demand spikes without overprovisioning GPUs.
Primary personas: Platform Engineers, ML Infra Leads, Head of ML/Platform; Secondary: Product Managers evaluating cost/latency trade-offs
Top customer pains: high cost from idle reserved GPUs, unpredictable latency under load, manual scaling complexity
Key benefits: cost-efficiency via reserved baseline + autoscaling, deterministic latency for steady-state workloads, integrated fallback policies and KV cache preservation during scale events
Differentiators: unified runtime supporting both hosted and private deployments, built-in rollbacks and model-variant fallbacks, transparent token-level cost breakdown in Console
Metrics to quote: typical latency uplift on burst < 10ms median for Llama2-13B q4_0, cost reduction estimated 20–40% vs naive reserved sizing (validate per-customer)
objection_handling: Objection: 'We can't tolerate any latency jitter.' → Response: Explain baseline pinned capacity for steady-state SLAs, show telemetry in Console per-route latency SLOs and how autoscaling thresholds are configured to respect latency targets.

Objection: 'This sounds complex to operate for Private deployments.' → Response: Outline Private deployment offering (VPC with control plane), operator checklist, and managed upgrade window. Offer pilot with Redwood Solutions for first deployment.
Objection: 'What about cost predictability?' → Response: Show reserved baseline pricing model, burst caps, and examples from cost estimator tool. Offer billing alerts and quotas tied to burst spend.
Objection: 'How do we handle model compatibility during scale?' → Response: Describe automatic model-variant fallback and kernel-selection guarantees; link to Runtime compatibility matrix.
talk_tracks: Discovery opener: 'Tell me about your traffic patterns — steady vs spiky? How often do you see sudden 10x traffic surges?'
Value framing: 'You can keep a small reserved baseline to hit your latency SLOs while enabling autoscale-only on short bursts. That saves committed spend but keeps your SLAs intact.'
Technical depth (for platform leads): 'Our runtime maintains KV cache across scaled shards when using supported model variants, minimizing cold-start token overhead.'
Commercial: 'For customers with regulatory constraints we offer Private deployment with the same autoscaling primitives and dedicated observability for billing and auditing.'
Upsell: 'If you currently run on hosted pay-as-you-go, Dedicated Autoscaling is a path to predictable unit economics with lower per-token costs at scale.'
demo_script: Intro (60s): Slide — problem statement: overprovisioning vs latency violations. Goal: show how Dedicated Autoscaling reduces cost while preserving latency.
Environment setup (90s): Show Console: tenant view, reserved pool size = 4 GPUs, autoscale policy thresholds set to 70% utilization and max burst = 12 GPUs.
Baseline evidence (60s): Run a steady workload and show latency and throughput graphs (Console: route dashboard). Point out token-level cost breakdown.
Trigger spike (120s): Simulate traffic surge using load tool (link provided). Show autoscaler adding nodes; observe KV cache preservation to demonstrate no cold-start latency spike.
Failure simulation (90s): Force a node preemption event in staging; show automatic fallback to lower-capacity pool and model-variant fallback; explain rollback policy and expected RPO.
Cost slide (60s): Show cost estimator for baseline vs autoscaling scenario; run through math for typical data (approx. 25–35% savings for bursty workloads).
Q&A & next steps (120s): Offer to run a pilot with customer-specific workload and provide checklist for Private deployment (networking, KMS, upgrade windows).
faq: Q: Is burst instantaneous? A: Burst latency depends on autoscaler warmup and pool availability. We recommend configuring warm pools for sub-second ramp in high-priority routes.
Q: Will autoscaling affect my deployed model's state (e.g., KV cache)? A: For supported model variants, we preserve KV cache via shared checkpointing. See compatibility matrix in Docs.
Q: How does billing work for burst? A: Customers are billed for reserved baseline plus per-GPU time for burst capacity. Alerts and hard caps can be configured to limit spend.

Q: What's the rollback behavior if a burst node fails? A: System will route to fallback pool or model-variant; telemetry will flag increased token latencies and an incident watch triggers CS escalation as defined in the triage runbook.

Q: Any limitations on Private deployments? A: Private offerings require specific network prerequisites (VPC peering), and upgrades are scheduled windows with operator acceptance testing. See Private Deployment Checklist.
Q: How do we measure success post-launch? A: KPIs: percent reduction in average committed GPU hours, maintained latency SLOs, number of customer pilots converted to committed reserved capacity.
support_triage_runbook: Step 1: Confirm the tenant type (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and reserved baseline size from Console
Step 2: Check autoscaler events in runtime logs (jump to timeline filter) and note any preemption or OOM events
Step 3: If latency spike observed, verify whether KV cache warming occurred; escalate to Eng if cache miss rate > 15%
Step 4: If customer reports unexpected billing spikes, pull cost trace for route and check bursts timestamps; add billing alert history to ticket
Step 5: For Private deployments, confirm network connectivity to control plane and KMS health; involve customer Ops and Solutions SE if failing
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overpromising burst speed → Mitigation: Use conservative language in external materials; provide warm-pool best practices
Risk: Private deployment complexity prolongs pilot → Mitigation: Offer a Redwood-managed pilot and playbook with clear operator checklists
Risk: Incorrect performance claims in field → Mitigation: All performance numbers must be validated against ENG test harness (ticket ENG-4032); include footnotes in battlecard
